title: VLM@school – Evaluation of AI image understanding on German middle school knowledge
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how well vision-language models (VLMs) can handle real educational multimodal tasks that require both image understanding and subject-specific background knowledge. The authors argue that existing benchmarks are often overly English-centric, too multiple-choice oriented, and insufficiently grounded in authentic classroom content. To stress-test models more realistically, they construct a new German benchmark based on middle school curriculum materials and related educational books.

The benchmark, VLM@school, contains 486 images and 2,038 open-ended questions across nine domains: arts, biology, geography, history, math, music, physics, religion, and sports. Questions were written by German native speakers, and some items were deliberately adversarial or required the model to say that the answer cannot be determined from the image. The evaluation compared thirteen open-weight VLMs using LLM-as-a-judge with a panel of judges to score open-ended responses.

The main finding is that even strong modern VLMs perform poorly on this kind of school-level, German-language multimodal reasoning task: the best model achieved under 45% overall accuracy, and adversarial questions were substantially harder. The results suggest that public benchmark performance does not necessarily transfer to educational multimodal understanding, especially when tasks are open-ended, non-English, and require careful integration of visual evidence with domain knowledge.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed benchmark evaluation with a clear dataset, protocol, and quantitative results, but it is not an educational intervention study and does not assess learner outcomes. The methodology is descriptive/diagnostic rather than causal, so it fits a lower-evidence correlational/benchmarking tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not test an educational intervention or demonstrate improvement in K-12 student learning outcomes. Its findings primarily show limitations of current VLMs on benchmark tasks, so there is no demonstrated instructional impact.

finding.finding_summary: The paper evaluates vision-language models on German middle-school subject knowledge using 486 images and 2,038 open-ended questions across nine domains. Accuracy is low overall: the best model reaches only 43.26% overall, and even domain bests are around 54% in history and religion, indicating substantial limitations in multimodal subject-specific understanding rather than student learning gains.
finding.measure: Open-ended benchmark accuracy on subject-specific image-question pairs

finding.finding_summary: The benchmark is designed to test integrated visual reasoning, background knowledge, and the ability to refuse unanswerable questions. Models perform especially poorly on adversarial questions, with overall accuracy ranging from 3.02% to 32.83% and the best model only 31.32% overall, showing weak performance on robust reasoning and uncertainty handling.
finding.study_size: n=2038 questions total; adversarial subset included
